name: Townhouse Gallery
funding: Small independent non-profit founded 1998 by William Wells, now a foundation; no funder list found and its website no longer resolves.
watch: Founded in 1998 as Egypt's first independent contemporary art space. It closed after a state raid in 2015, then ran from a converted factory.
records_note: The gallery's own website no longer resolves and no official page was found, so its reports, accounts, funders and board could not be checked.

name: Transmission Gallery
funding: Creative Scotland, member subscriptions, grassroots fundraisers.
watch: Artist-run cooperative founded in 1983 by Glasgow School of Art graduates as an alternative to commercial galleries and municipal conservatism. Run by a rotating, unpaid artist committee.

name: Typography Center for Contemporary Art
watch: Independent contemporary art center founded in 2012 by the artist group ZIP; it also ran the KICA school.

name: Uffizi
funding: State museum under the Ministry of Culture. Donors include Veronica Atkins (€4.5M, Boboli amphitheatre), Edwin L. Wiegand Foundation ($1M, Vasari Corridor), Ferragamo (€600k, 2014) and Fondazione CR Firenze.
watch: Contract workers protested before Botticelli's Venus on 5 April 2026 over outsourced jobs. Climate activists hit its paintings in 2022 and 2024; no funder targeted.
records_note: No annual report; its transparency portal posts accounts for 2023 to 2026 and a five-member board, and the donation page names donors, mostly undated.

name: Ulaanbaatar International Media Art Festival (UBIMAF)
funding: Run by the Arts Council of Mongolia, an NGO. Backers named: Goethe-Institut (2016, 2022), Asia-Europe Foundation, US Embassy and Xacbank (2016), Taiwan Foundation for Democracy (2022). Later editions name none.
watch: The 9th edition ran in May 2024 at the Mongolian National Art Gallery and Red Ger Gallery under the theme Seeing is Believing.
records_note: Its organiser, the Arts Council of Mongolia, posts reports 2003 to 2024 and names its governing council; no accounts or funder list.

name: Urban Shaman Contemporary Aboriginal Art
funding: Small artist-run centre; Canada Council gave $280k over two years (2017-18); also Manitoba Arts Council, Winnipeg Arts Council and Province of Manitoba.
watch: Indigenous artist-run centre founded in 1996 in the Exchange District.
records_note: T3010 returns sit on the CRA charity listing; the site names three directors and shows nine undated, unlabelled supporter logos; no annual reports.

name: Van Abbemuseum
funding: Eindhoven municipality, Mondriaan Fund, Ammodo, Creative Europe and the Promotors foundation; VriendenLoterij, a public charity lottery, is also listed as a supporter.
watch: Runs the 'Deviant Practice' research programme, which reads the collection archives from decolonial, queer and disability-inclusive perspectives. In 2021 it adopted a climate and ethics manifesto barring sponsors from carbon-intensive, arms-manufacturing or human-rights-flagged entities.
records_note: It names funds and donors on undated pages, but posts only 2012 and 2013 annual reports, no accounts and no board.

name: Vasl Artists' Association
funding: Non-profit company limited by guarantee. Its 2026 disclosure lists COMO Museum of Art, Khurram Kasim Art Foundation, HUM TV, HBL Art Committee, Kadist, AFIELD and private collectors.
watch: Runs residencies and exhibitions in Karachi; over 500 artists have taken part in 25 years.
records_note: Names its board and supporters in a 2026 disclosure; posts no annual report, and says audited accounts exist but does not publish them.

name: Vleeshal Center for Contemporary Art
funding: City of Middelburg, Mondriaan Fund, Province of Zeeland. Complete public accounting under Dutch ANBI non-profit guidelines.
watch: The Province of Zeeland, named in the first draft, is not listed there.
records_note: Vleeshal posts annual reports and accounts for 2019 to 2025, names its supervisory board, and names its two public funders on an undated page.

name: W139
funding: Public subsidies from Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst (AFK) and Mondriaan Fund, artist dues, and foundation grants. Zero commercial gallery representation.

name: Wattis Institute
funding: Part of California College of the Arts. Donate page lists the Horace W. Goldsmith and Richard foundations, San Francisco Grants for the Arts, and individual donors.
watch: Non-profit research institute and contemporary gallery at CCA.
records_note: No records of its own; parent CCA lists trustees and files 990s on ProPublica, and the Wattis donate page names supporters undated.

name: West Den Haag
funding: Mondriaan Fund, City of The Hague, non-profit cultural trusts. Fully audited accounts published annually.
